name: vscode-bazel-java
description: Imports Bazel java targets into the Java Language Server using bazel aquery

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Importing a Bazel workspace runs bazel, which evaluates the repository's own BUILD and .bzl files as code.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Requires a real filesystem and a bazel binary that can be executed against it.

bazelJava.binary.markdownDescription: Absolute path to the bazel or bazelisk binary. When empty, PATH is searched. Machine-scoped on purpose: this path is executed, so a repository must not be able to set it.

bazelJava.targets.markdownDescription: Target patterns to import, for example `//services/...`. Empty means the whole repository, or the `directories:` block of `.bazelproject` when `#bazelJava.useBazelProject#` is on. Narrowing this is the single biggest win on a large monorepo.

bazelJava.excludeTargets.markdownDescription: Target patterns to subtract from the imported set, for example `//platform/infra/...`.

bazelJava.useBazelProject.markdownDescription: Read the import scope from the `directories:` block of `.bazelproject` when `#bazelJava.targets#` is empty.

bazelJava.importMode.markdownDescription: `lazy` imports the configured scope and, when a java file outside it is opened, provisions that one package on demand. `eager` imports the configured scope and nothing else. With no scope configured the two are identical, since everything is already in scope.

bazelJava.projectLayout.markdownDescription: Where a generated project's directory lives. `metadata` keeps it in the language server's own storage and writes nothing into your working copy. Set it to `repository` if you want the Spring Tools index - beans, endpoints, live hovers, the `@` symbol searches: that indexer reads a source folder as *project location + entry path*, so with the `metadata` layout it looks at directories that do not exist and finds nothing. `repository` puts the project directory at the bazel package its targets come from, which makes those paths real. The Spring Boot Dashboard's list of applications does not need this. Class output stays in the language server's storage either way, so the working copy is still untouched. A project whose directory would contain another project's keeps the `metadata` layout. Changing this recreates the projects and costs one reindex.

bazelJava.maxProjects.description: Safety valve. Above this many projects the import is capped and a warning is logged, since each project costs an Eclipse project plus a classpath container.

bazelJava.groupSourceRoots.markdownDescription: Merge the `src/main` and `src/test` targets of one package into a single project with two source folders. Turning this off restores one project per target.

bazelJava.buildOnImport.markdownDescription: `aquery` reports the jars a build *would* consume, not jars that are current. A jar produced before its inputs last changed is still on disk and gets indexed, so the IDE shows a stale API - a field added last week reads as `undefined` while `bazel build` succeeds. `background` builds the imported targets once per session to keep them current (incremental, so a no-op on an up-to-date repository). `off` never builds; use `JBazel: Build Classpath` by hand.

bazelJava.discoveryNoFetch.markdownDescription: Pass `--nofetch` to the discovery query so indexing never reaches the network. An unreachable container registry then fails the loading phase instantly instead of hanging, and the java targets still come back.

bazelJava.commandTimeoutSeconds.description: Timeout for a single bazel query or aquery. Short on purpose: a hung query must not hang the IDE.

bazelJava.noblockForLock.markdownDescription: Fail fast and retry shortly when another bazel command - usually a terminal build - holds the server lock, instead of queueing behind it for the whole build. Applies `--noblock_for_lock` to the IDE's bazel invocations; the status bar shows when the IDE is waiting. Turn off to restore queueing.

bazelJava.backoffMaxSeconds.description: Upper bound of the exponential backoff applied after a failed import, so a broken or offline workspace is retried at a decreasing rate instead of continuously.

bazelJava.outputBase.markdownDescription: Set to `ide` to give the IDE its own bazel server under `~/.cache/bazel-ide/<hash>`, or to an absolute path. This stops the IDE and the terminal from blocking each other on the bazel server lock and lets the IDE shut its own server down on exit. Costs a second analysis cache (1-2 GB). Empty means share the developer's server. Machine-scoped: it becomes a `--output_base` startup option.

bazelJava.maxIdleSeconds.markdownDescription: `--max_idle_secs` for the IDE-owned bazel server. Only applies when `#bazelJava.outputBase#` is set.

bazelJava.buildJobs.markdownDescription: `--jobs` for the builds this extension starts by itself. `0` leaves bazel's own default, which is every core - right for a build you are waiting on, wrong for one the indexer started behind your back on the machine you are typing on.

bazelJava.mavenRepository.markdownDescription: Name of the external repository holding the third-party artifacts, as `MODULE.bazel` names it. Used only by **JBazel: Fetch Library Sources** to find the source jars to download.
